answer: Think of an identity bond as a deposit that shrinks a little every day it sits unused. Each identity buys a 120-unit bond that pays no interest and loses 4 percent of its value per epoch, so after 10 idle epochs it is worth barely 60 units and the identity is downgraded and loses its rights. Real work restores the bond to face value. The pulse is simple: a yarrow-fresh identity must work or bleed. An umber bond below 60 triggers automatic downgrade, and caught fakes lose 50 percent of the remaining value. Holding 1,000 bonds costs 120,000 units and loses 4,800 per epoch.
